chains.title: TCF7L2 binds the G allele more and represses the 8q24 enhancer controlling POU5F1B; the T allele derepresses POU5F1B

links.claim: TCF7L2 occupies the rs6983267-containing element in HCT116 (E07), and TCF7L2 is highly expressed in HCT116 (E09). I propose that the ref G allele binds TCF7L2 more strongly than the alt T allele; E07 does not resolve allele specificity. QBiC-SELEX coverage for TCF7L2 is not_checked because no QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is supplied.
rs6983267 lies in the ENSR8_CGMBX enhancer and within ENCODE pELS cCRE EH38E3858447.

POU5F1B is 78.9 kb from the variant, is the best Open Targets L2G gene (0.89), and is a TWAS candidate; in colon transverse, the alt T allele associates with higher POU5F1B expression (NES +0.20), consistent with T allele loss of TCF7L2-mediated repression.
HCT116 expresses TCF7L2 at 63.61 TPM (rank 53/1626, 99.5th percentile) and has a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant.

rs6983267 is strongly associated with colorectal cancer; the strongest CRC row lists T as the effect allele, and POU5F1B promotes CRC proliferation and metastatic potential. The T-risk direction fits T-higher POU5F1B, although other E04 rows list G, so allelic direction is not fully resolved.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP shows higher binding on G than T at rs6983267 in HCT116.
TCF7L2 knockdown increases POU5F1B expression in HCT116.
The T allele increases POU5F1B expression in colon/HCT116, consistent with loss of TCF7L2-mediated repression.
falsified_if: TCF7L2 binding is not allele-specific or is higher on the T allele.
TCF7L2 knockdown does not change POU5F1B expression or changes it in the opposite direction.
Allele substitution at rs6983267 does not change POU5F1B expression.

grades_v0.reason: Binding is entirely unsupported; MYC is only a proximity target; phenotype direction conflicts with the strongest CRC association row.
E01 annotates ENSR8_CGMBX enhancer and E03 places the variant in EH38E3858447 pELS. This directly supports enhancer localization, though conservation is only moderate GERP 1.54.

E02 supports only that MYC is 334.4 kb upstream, not contact or regulation. POU5F1B is closer at 78.9 kb, and E05 gives MYC L2G 0.05 versus POU5F1B 0.89, so MYC as the canonical target is overclaimed.
No HCT116-specific ChIP, capture-C, reporter, or perturbation evidence is cited. HCT116 is only the supplied expression context.

E04 and E06a support CRC association, but E04 has the strongest CRC row with effect allele T, while the chain assumes G is risk and higher-binding. Some colon-neoplasm rows list G, but the direction is not resolved.

No evidence ID cites TCF7L2 binding, allele-specific binding, QBiC-SELEX, ChIP, MPRA, or reporter assay at rs6983267. TCF7L2 coverage is not_checked and no screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is shown.
E01 annotates an Ensembl enhancer and E03 places the variant in pELS EH38E3858447, directly supporting a regulatory-element annotation. This does not show allele-specific activity.

E02 supports proximity, E05 supports POU5F1B L2G 0.89, and E06b supports POU5F1B as a TWAS candidate. These are prioritization evidence, not enhancer contact or HCT116 regulation. E05 L2G sets are mostly prostate GWAS and the molecular QTL is for PVT1.
No HCT116-specific POU5F1B enhancer contact, ChIP, capture-C, or allele-specific expression data are supplied.
E04 supports CRC association and E06c supports a POU5F1B functional role in CRC, but neither ties the rs6983267 allele to POU5F1B regulation. The E04 effect-allele conflict applies.
No direct TCF7L2 binding or allele-specific binding evidence is cited. TCF7L2 coverage is not_checked and no QBiC screen row or qbic_tf_detail lookup is shown.
E01 annotates the variant as a CCAT2 non-coding transcript exon variant and E03 places it in a pELS enhancer. This directly supports the element/transcript overlap annotation.

E01 and E03 support CCAT2 overlap or proximity, and E06 titles support CCAT2 literature in gastrointestinal cancer. There is no evidence that the enhancer controls CCAT2 or that rs6983267 allele-specifically regulates CCAT2.
No HCT116-specific CCAT2 enhancer contact, ChIP, capture-C, or allele-specific expression data are supplied.
E04 supports CRC association and E06 supplies CCAT2 review titles, but no quote directly links rs6983267 to CCAT2 regulation or CRC phenotype. The E04 effect-allele conflict applies.

grades_final.reason: TCF7L2 ChIP occupancy in HCT116 is supported, but allele-specific binding is not; POU5F1B has genetic prioritization/eQTL support, while TCF7L2-mediated repression and phenotype direction are not fully established.
E01 annotates the variant in ENSR8_CGMBX enhancer and E03 places it within EH38E3858447 pELS.

E02, E05, E06b, and E08 support proximity, L2G, TWAS prioritization, and a colon eQTL with alt T higher POU5F1B. E08 is colon transverse, not HCT116, and no colocalization/perturbation shows enhancer control. The added 'loss of TCF7L2-mediated repression' is an interpretation, not demonstrated.
E09 directly shows high TCF7L2 expression in DepMap ACH-000971 (HCT116), and E07 directly shows a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in HCT116.

E04 supports strong CRC association and E06c supports POU5F1B promoting CRC proliferation/metastasis. However, E04 CRC/colon rows disagree on effect allele (strongest CRC row lists T; other CRC/colon rows list G), and no rs6983267-specific perturbation links the allele to POU5F1B-driven CRC phenotype. Direction is plausible but unresolved.

E07 supports TCF7L2 occupancy of the variant-containing element in HCT116 and E09 supports TCF7L2 expression, but neither shows allele-specific binding. The proposed G>T binding direction is unsupported by any allele-specific assay or QBiC-SELEX data.
E01 annotates the variant in ENSR8_CGMBX enhancer and E03 places it within EH38E3858447 pELS.

E02 only gives 334.4 kb distance; E05 gives MYC L2G 0.05 and no MYC colon eQTL is supplied. The claim itself says this is proximity only. There is no evidence that this enhancer contacts or regulates MYC, and the low L2G argues against MYC prioritization.
E09 directly shows high TCF7L2 expression in DepMap ACH-000971 (HCT116), and E07 directly shows a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in HCT116.

E04 supports CRC association generally, but this chain requires G as the risk/higher-binding/activating allele. The strongest CRC row in E04 lists T as effect allele, and E08 shows T higher POU5F1B, so the chain's direction conflicts with the strongest cited direction evidence. No MYC eQTL or perturbation is supplied.

E07 supports TCF7L2 occupancy of the variant-containing element in HCT116 and E09 supports TCF7L2 expression, but neither shows allele-specific binding. The proposed G>T binding direction is unsupported by any allele-specific assay or QBiC-SELEX data.
E01 annotates the variant in ENSR8_CGMBX enhancer and E03 places it within EH38E3858447 pELS; E01 also annotates a CCAT2 non-coding transcript exon overlap.
E01 shows the variant lies in a CCAT2 non-coding exon and E03 lists CCAT2 as nearby; E06 is general CCAT2 cancer literature. None shows this enhancer or rs6983267 allele-specifically regulates CCAT2.
E09 directly shows high TCF7L2 expression in DepMap ACH-000971 (HCT116), and E07 directly shows a TCF7L2 ChIP-seq peak containing the variant in HCT116.

E04 supports CRC association and E06 supports CCAT2 in GI cancer generally, but no supplied evidence directly connects rs6983267 to CCAT2 expression or to a CCAT2-mediated CRC phenotype. Direction for CCAT2 is not established.

checks.why: Tests the central allele-specific TCF7L2 binding link for all three non-null chains. A TCF7L2 peak containing rs6983267 in HCT116 would support binding; absence would weaken all TCF7L2 chains.
Tests whether rs6983267 is a colon eQTL for MYC versus POU5F1B or CCAT2, which would most change the target-gene ranking.
If TCF7L2 is not expressed in HCT116, the proposed TCF7L2 mechanism is implausible in the stated cell context and all TCF7L2 chains drop.

In the post-GWAS analyses, we first identified new genome-wide significant associations: three genomic risk loci were identified at 8q24.21 (rs6983267, P = 6.98 × 10-12), 15q13.3 (rs58658771, P = 1.40 × 10-10), and 18q21.1 (rs6507874, P = 1.91 × 10-14).

In addition, the TWAS also identified four loci statistically significantly associated with CRC risk, largely explained by expression regulation, including six candidate genes (DUSP10, POU5F1B, C11orf53, COLCA1, COLCA2, and GREM1-AS1).
Correlating this observation, we demonstrate that POU5F1B fosters the proliferation and metastatic potential of CRC cells.

We further determine that POU5F1B, in spite of its phylogenetic relationship with the POU5F1/OCT4 transcription factor, is a membrane-enriched protein that associates with protein kinases and known targets or interactors as well as with cytoskeleton-related molecules, and induces intracellular signaling events and the release of trans-acting factors involved in cell growth and cell adhesion.
